# Wolfpack

> Self-hosted browser terminal manager for AI coding agents running on your own macOS/Linux machines.

Wolfpack is a PWA and CLI for controlling long-running terminal sessions from a phone or browser. It is built for AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, shell commands, and custom agent wrappers. Sessions run locally through a Rust PTY broker; Wolfpack does not provide a hosted relay or account service. Remote access is typically handled through Tailscale.

## Core topics

- AI agent terminal orchestrator
- Browser terminal dashboard
- Mobile control for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and shell sessions
- Self-hosted remote development over Tailscale
- Persistent PTY sessions owned by a local broker
- Multi-machine session list and desktop terminal grid

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/almogdepaz/wolfpack/main/install.sh | bash
wolfpack
```

npm alternatives:

```bash
bunx wolfpack-bridge
npx wolfpack-bridge
```

## Security model summary

Wolfpack is self-hosted software for machines you control. Treat access to Wolfpack like shell access to that machine. The browser talks to the local Wolfpack server over HTTP/WebSocket, the server talks to the broker over a per-user Unix socket, and the broker owns PTYs and runs commands locally in selected project directories. Optional JWT auth can be layered on top of Tailscale.
